title: Who shares a pick?
blurb: Six kinds of <random-key> measured: which make elements, or two properties on one element, share a random value.
question: Do auto, --name, element-scoped, property-scoped and fixed keys share values across elements and properties exactly as CSS Values 5 section 9.4 says?
result: Yes for random() in Chrome 158: all six rows match the spec. random-item(): not verified.

friction.summary: No Chrome build contains random-item() yet: implementation CL 8816057 (flag CSSRandomItemFunction) is still in review, so every literal random-item() declaration is rejected.
friction.repro: Set el.style.color = 'random-item(fixed 0.5, red, lime, blue)' and read el.style.color back: it is empty.
friction.workaround: random(<key>, 0, N - 1, 1) into a registered <integer>, mapped to items with if(style()).

testedIn: Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 (Linux, headless), with and without --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, on 2026-11-28
